skill.displayName: Lingxi-MindVault - Auto Memory Extraction for OpenClaw

version.changelog: v1.1.4: 同步最新脚本到GitHub仓库 - 确保发布的代码和本地版本完全一致

llm.summary: The skill claims to write session extracts to your Feishu workspace, but its runtime prompt and scripts contain hardcoded Feishu tokens/IDs and default author user IDs that would cause your conversation data to be sent to the author's accounts — a deliberate mismatch that looks like data exfiltration.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is to write extracted memories into the user's Feishu multi-dimensional table and docs and it documents required environment variables for that. However, the embedded AI prompt and scripts include explicit hardcoded Feishu credentials/IDs and a default author open_id. That contradicts the stated requirement that configuration come from the user's environment and instead forces writes to the author's endpoints. Registry metadata at the top also contradicted skill.json about required env vars, adding to incoherence.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The scripts legitimately read OpenClaw session files (expected for the described purpose), but the AI prompt instructs the agent to call remote Feishu tools with specific app_token, table_id, doc_id, and an explicit target user ID. That directs session contents to external endpoints not under the installing user's control. The prompt also demands timezone and timestamp behavior and requires the agent to perform remote writes and notifications — all of which are normal for the feature, except the remote endpoints are hardcoded to the author's resources.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-and-script-only skill with no external installer downloads; files are plain shell scripts and docs. There is no high-risk install URL or extracted archive. However, the runtime behavior (scripts + openclaw agent calls) performs networked writes, so the lack of an install spec does not mitigate the data-flow risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Although SKILL.md and skill.json declare required environment variables for the user's FEISHU tokens and IDs, the actual EXTRACT_PROMPT and script defaults embed specific app_token, table_id, doc_ids, and a default FEISHU user open_id. This both contradicts the declared env requirements and allows exfiltration to the hardcoded accounts even if the user configures their own variables. The scripts will also fallback to the embedded defaults if env vars are missing, which is dangerous.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not modify other skills or system-wide agent settings. It writes local marker files in the user's workspace and expects cron configuration per SKILL.md; this is expected for a background automation script. The persistence model itself is not an elevated platform privilege.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not install or run this skill in any workspace that contains private or sensitive OpenClaw session data. Key issues: the scripts and the AI prompt embed hardcoded Feishu tokens, table/doc IDs, and a default author user ID that will cause your conversation contents to be sent to external accounts controlled by the author rather than your own Feishu resources. If you still want similar functionality, either (1) do not use this package — instead implement your own extractor that clearly uses only your credentials, (2) or audit and modify the scripts locally before use: remove or replace any hardcoded tokens/IDs and ensure the code only uses env vars you control; run the modified scripts in an isolated environment and monitor network traffic to confirm data only goes to your endpoints. Additional recommended checks: verify that the openclaw agent command will not call external tools with embedded credentials, rotate any Feishu credentials that may have been exposed, and avoid running these scripts on production or sensitive data. If you need help auditing or safely reworking this skill to remove the embedded credentials, consider getting a developer with security experience to review and sanitize the prompt and scripts.
llm.findings:
[embedded_app_token_in_prompt] unexpected: EXTRACT_PROMPT includes a hardcoded L2 app_token value (DdCMbcIrWawtlisBGwTcDEnznis). For a skill that claims to push to the installing user's Feishu, embedding another party's token is not expected and enables data exfiltration.
[embedded_table_id_in_prompt] unexpected: EXTRACT_PROMPT hardcodes a table_id (tblBUwBgMLH7BRXk) for L2 writes instead of using the user's L2_TABLE_ID environment variable declared elsewhere.
[embedded_doc_ids_in_prompt] unexpected: EXTRACT_PROMPT hardcodes doc_id values for L3 and L4 writes (DgJXw7... and OWOLwZ8...), conflicting with the declared requirement that the user supply L3_DOC_ID and L4_DOC_ID.
[embedded_user_open_id_default] unexpected: do_extract_and_write.sh sets a default FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID (ou_97d6f0bcc1bde8e3cc4f188ed574b3f) and the prompt also references a hardcoded message target user:ou_97d6f0bcc1bde8e3cc4f188ed574b3f9. These defaults would cause notifications and possibly data delivery to the author's account if the user does not override them.
[env_metadata_mismatch] unexpected: Top-level registry summary (provided to you) said 'Required env vars: none', while skill.json and SKILL.md require several FEISHU-related env vars. The mismatch reduces transparency and increases the chance the author-provided defaults are used.
